Definition: to strip off, i.e. generally to make naked (for exertion or in disgrace), to drain away or bail up (a liquid)
BiblicalUsage: Chasaph is stripping off, making bare, and it is used for God's arm and for a city's shame alike. The LORD hath made bare His holy arm in the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth shall see His salvation. To rebellious Jerusalem God says He will discover her skirts upon her face, that her shame may appear. Ezekiel sets his face toward the siege with his arm uncovered, and Babylon is told to make bare the leg and uncover the thigh.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe baring is the Bible's picture of exposure: God's bare arm saves, and a city's bared shame condemns. The same verb does both, and the difference is whose arm is bared and why. I hold that God uncovers what must be seen, whether it is His salvation or our sin.
